Hi all — attaching the brief tech note (network_requirements.xlsx) and the initial prompt template set (prompt_templates_v1.md). High level answers below; happy to walk through on call.

Auth & SDK notes:
- Recommended: API-key over PrivateLink for quick POC; for production with VPC requirements use PrivateLink + API-key. We support mTLS in Private deployments; for hosted we recommend API-key + PrivateLink/VPC peering.
- Token rotation: short-lived tokens + KMS-backed signing. Redwood SDK supports automatic rotation hooks and integration with AWS KMS and customer-managed HSMs.
- Example (pseudo):
  - SDK init: redwood.Client(api_key=env.REDWOOD_KEY, region='us-west-2', private_link=true)
  - Auth flow: backend exchanges long-lived credential for short-lived session token; SDK uses session token for calls.

Routing & embeddings/reranker:
- For 200k items, 1536-dim embeddings are a good baseline (we also support 768 options with quantized indexes).
- Architecture: ingestion -> embedding store (Pinecone/FAISS) -> candidate retrieval -> lightweight reranker (fine-tuned cross-encoder) as a second pass.
- Reindexing: incremental workflows supported via update APIs; for frequent writes use batched async updates and background merging.
- Latency: aim for <100ms candidate retrieval and <150-250ms for reranker depending on model size; suggest async fallback to cached results for cold-start queries.

Structured output & tool-calling:
- SDK supports structured output schemas and function/tool calling (post-processing hooks). Use strict JSON schema validation on the server to reject invalid outputs and log mismatches to the audit trail.

Prompt templates & governance:
- Versioning: treat prompt templates as code — store in Git with tags/PRs; each deployed prompt gets an immutable prompt_id and semantic version. Redwood supports binding a prompt_id to a model route so rollbacks are easy.
- Injection mitigations: multi-layer strategy:
  1) System-level forcing: set an immutable system prompt on the server that takes precedence over user content.
  2) Input sanitization: escape or strip user content where it shouldn't be executed (especially for tool calls).
  3) Output validation: JSON schema enforcement for structured outputs; use classifiers to detect anomalous responses.
  4) Rate-limiting / anomaly detection for unusual prompt shapes.
- Red-team plan: have internal and partner red-team exercises quarterly. Use synthetic adversarial inputs, monitor model behavior, and add mitigations to the prompt template (e.g., explicit instructions, refusal patterns). Keep a changelog for prompt edits and weekly regression tests against a baseline eval set.

Attachments in the drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0A1acme-shared (contains the example SDK snippets and templates).

If this looks good I can produce a short example repo with SDK init, sample calls for embeddings + reranker wiring, and a prompt governance README.

–Dev
